headline: All majors below the 200-day line; longs crowded and bleeding; whales withdrawing Bitcoin while stablecoin powder shrinks.
paragraphs: The regime is fully down. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have posted a golden cross. The only structural upside signal in the majors is a narrow one: BNB and Doge both have MACD above signal line, and ADA's RSI sits at 55.7, just into neutral territory. Everything else is momentum in retreat. Bitcoin's RSI is 43.6, Ethereum's is 50.6, and the median across the group is sub-50. Price action reflects this: Bitcoin is down 0.22 percent on the day and 5.14 percent over the past week. Ethereum flat on the day but down 3.74 percent weekly. Solana off 1.24 percent and 7.76 percent respectively. These are not the patterns of accumulation; they are the footprints of steady selling pressure against a downtrend that has no visible floor.

Leverage positioning reveals acute crowding on the long side. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio on OKX is 2.13 to 1. Ethereum is 2.17 to 1. Solana is 2.92 to 1. XRP sits at 3.22 to 1, and Doge is at 4.98 to 1, the most extreme skew in the set. These are not marginal imbalances; they represent substantial unhedged conviction in a market that has already delivered a 49.8 percent drawdown in Bitcoin from its 12-month high of 124,740 dollars. Funding rates tell the other half of the story. Bitcoin is paying 0.44 basis points every eight hours to hold a long (4.8 percent annualized), and Solana is at 0.34 basis points (3.7 percent). Those are not cheap, but they are stable enough that the longs are not panicking yet. What matters more is the liquidation tape: in the past 24 hours, Bitcoin has seen 233 liquidations totaling 1.02 million dollars in long value against only 392,824 dollars in shorts. Ethereum is worse: 364 liquidations with 1.57 million dollars in long wipeouts and just 85,988 dollars in shorts. Solana has liquidated 1.25 million dollars in long positions and zero in shorts. The market is grinding long positions into powder.

Flows show two distinct moves happening in parallel. Whales have withdrawn 85.86 million dollars in Bitcoin off exchanges over the past 48 hours, with the largest single transfer being 157.5 million dollars out of Coinbase and 116.8 million dollars out of Kraken. That is classic long-term holder behavior: taking coins off the board during fear. But Ethereum flows contradict this narrative sharply. Over the same window, 8.63 million dollars in Ethereum flowed back onto exchanges, with Coinbase Institutional receiving 68.3 million dollars and Coinbase retail taking another bite. This divergence between Bitcoin accumulation and Ethereum distribution is a tension worth watching. Bitcoin's ETF flow on July 31st was negative 265.4 million dollars, a heavy single-session print, though the five-session rolling net is only negative 61.5 million dollars with same-direction days at 1. Ethereum's ETF flow was positive 9.0 million dollars on the same day, and the five-session net is positive 10.0 million dollars with same-direction days at 2. The traditional finance bid for Bitcoin is hesitant; Ethereum interest persists slightly, though the overall regime has not rotated.

Stablecoin float has shrunk 1.63 percent over the past month and now sits at 303.9 billion dollars. That is a meaningful erosion of dry powder at a time when the crowd's fear gauge reads 27, near the bottom of its recent 20 to 33 range. When stablecoins decline while prices fall, the market is burning through reserve capital to support bids rather than accumulating it to catch the knife. The whale stablecoin buying power metric is negative 354.2 million dollars over 48 hours, meaning more stables left exchanges than arrived. This is not the signature of preparation; it is the signature of deployment in real time against weakness. Solana's open interest of 213 million dollars is small and crowded long, while Bitcoin's 1.98 billion dollars in perp open interest is substantial and tilted long. Both conditions invite instability if prices move lower.

Sentiment sits in fear at 27, and the tape confirms that the crowd is right to be uncomfortable. Price sits 49.8 percent below Bitcoin's 12-month high. The majors have spent weeks below their moving averages without relief. Long liquidations outnumber shorts by orders of magnitude across every major pair. The only counterweight in the data is whale Bitcoin accumulation and the faint MACD divergence in BNB, Doge, and ADA, but divergence is not yet reversal; it is merely exhaustion of the bearish momentum. Watch for a golden cross to form in any major, for the long-to-short ratio on Bitcoin to fall below 1.8 to 1, or for stablecoin float to stabilize and begin rising. Those conditions would tell you the tape has shifted. Until then, the message is clear: the market remains in a structural downtrend with a crowded long-side bet that is losing money on the daily.
